text:
OCCURS LINK MEASURED BY THE CHIEF. IT DOES NOT FIRE. Bead stays P2; do NOT promote it,
and do NOT thread Option through the consumers as if this were a live bug.

I filed this with reachability explicitly unmeasured and then went and measured it, because
I had written the promotion criterion and nobody was on it. I expected to promote it. I was
wrong, and the negative result is worth more than the promotion would have been.

WHAT I EXPECTED. StorySourceView builds `nodes` (and therefore `index`) by flat-mapping
sourceSupport, while `known` and `narratedWorldSituations` are built from `all` -- so I
expected `all` to be the wider set, adjacency and worldOrder to carry refs absent from
`index`, and node(ref) to miss. worldOrder even guards it in place at :268 with
`index.get(r).map(_.discoursePosition).getOrElse(0)`, which reads exactly like an author
who had been bitten.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE, StorySourceView.scala:65-66:

  private val all: Vector[NarrativeNodeId] =
    allNarrative.filter(n => source.sourceSupport(n).nonEmpty)

`all` is ALREADY filtered to supported nodes. So nodes, index, known and
narratedWorldSituations share ONE domain, and unsupported nodes never become refs at all --
they are captured separately in the `dropped` field with a reason. node(ref) is total over
every ref this view exposes. The guard at :268 is defensive and unreachable, as is the
getOrElse(0.0) in relativePosition, by this route. InMemorySourceView has the same shape:
index is built from nodes and refs come from nodes.

The only surviving route is textLength == 0, which needs an empty source text. I searched
for a construction with a literal 0 and found none.

SO THE CHAIN IS: permits YES, occurs NO, consumes YES (new-engineer traced it forward to
TransitionFeatures, RecallSignature, PopulationAggregate and embed-bench). Permits plus
consumes without occurs is a mutation surviving because the corpus cannot reach it -- which
is precisely the thing I wrote a rule about this morning, and I nearly published it as a
finding by assuming the middle link.

THE FIX IS STILL CORRECT, FOR A DIFFERENT AND SMALLER REASON. `discoursePos: SourceNodeRef
=> Option[Double] = r => Some(view.relativePosition(r))` declares an absence channel it can
never use, one line above a worldPos that uses the same channel properly. That is a false
declaration whether or not a caller trips it, and the next caller inherits it.

AND HERE IS THE PART THAT MATTERS MOST, WHICH THE MEASUREMENT ONLY MADE VISIBLE BY FAILING:
the safety is an ACCIDENT OF TWO IMPLEMENTATIONS, NOT A GUARANTEE OF THE INTERFACE.
SourceView is a public trait. Nothing in it says node(ref) must be total over the refs the
view exposes, or that adjacency and worldOrder may not mention a ref outside the node index.
Both current implementations happen to satisfy it; a third that does not would make every
consumer of relativePosition silently wrong, and no test would fail.

RECOMMENDED SHAPE for whoever takes this: write the invariant down as part of the SourceView
contract and assert it as a law over both implementations plus the generators, rather than
changing consumer signatures. That converts an accident into a guarantee and costs nothing
downstream. If the invariant is later deliberately broken, THEN the Option threading becomes
necessary and the law will say so at the moment it stops holding.
